correctness.rationale: For constant-preserving scalar linear interpolation, the exact oscillation seminorm at old point i is T_i=(|alpha_i-1|+sum_{j!=i}|alpha_j|)/2. If P=sum positive parts alpha_j, normalizing those positive parts gives a nonnegative probability vector with no larger T_i for any i (check separately p_i<=1 and p_i>1). For nonnegative alpha, constraints 1-alpha_i<=c*r_i are jointly feasible iff F(c)=sum_i(1-c*r_i)_+<=1; its max-over-subsets form reduces to the k smallest radii, yielding Lambda=max(1,max_{k>=2}(k-1)/R_k). Positive weights realize the universal Banach extension; the half-l1 zero-sum target with f_i=e_i-e_n forces the exact same minimax lower bound for arbitrary Banach extensions. F(Lambda)=1 if Lambda>1 enforces unique nonnegative coefficients. Pairwise triangle constraints prove Lambda<=2-2/n for n>=3, equality only all r_i=1/2. Independent scipy/HiGHS LP checked 167 valid random rational metric tuples n<=9 to error <=2.23e-16; finite numeric tests do not prove all real radii.
